- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent high or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.75) and price is trending up, model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.75), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; align forecast toward recent 5-day average rather than 30-day trend.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often fails to adjust; add 1–2 day lag correction or use 7-day rolling mean for short-term forecasting.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is negative or neutral, model tends to forecast higher than true; apply 3–5% downward adjustment for negative sentiment periods.
